sections.h2: Who collects property tax in Fulton County
sections.html:
Town collectors take current county and town tax early in the year. After that, the Fulton County Treasurer takes over whatever is still unpaid. The Treasurer's office is in the County Office Building at 223 West Main Street, Room 202, Johnstown, NY 12095, phone (518) 736-5580. Hours are Monday to Friday, 9 am to 5 pm, and 9 am to 4 pm from July 1 through Labor Day.

The Treasurer collects delinquent school, village, town and county taxes and runs the foreclosure and auction process under the state Real Property Tax Law. It works alongside the town tax collectors. It also collects and enforces taxes on parcels in the City of Gloversville, but it does not collect City of Johnstown taxes, so a Johnstown owner pays the city.

The Real Property Tax Service Agency, at (518) 736-5507 in the same building, keeps the tax maps. Its online Beacon map shows ownership, property inventory and assessed value, refreshed nightly. It also gives the parcel's SBL (section, block, lot) number, the same number printed on tax bills and assessment rolls. Look yours up before you call anyone, because every office will ask for it.

sections.h2: Payment windows and where to pay
sections.html:
Each tax has its own window. County and town tax is due early in the year, school and village tax come in the fall, and the City of Gloversville keeps its own calendar.

Fulton County payment windows
TaxPay toWindow
County and townTown collectorJanuary 1 to March 31
Unpaid county and townCounty TreasurerReturned April 1, collections begin May 1
VillageVillage collectorJune 1 to October 31
School (town districts)School tax collectorSeptember 1 to October 31
City of GloversvilleCity, then TreasurerApril 1 to October 31, Treasurer from December 1

Village and school payments are not accepted after October 31, and unpaid town, school and village amounts are relevied on the next county bill. Current county tax cannot be paid during the first two weeks of April while the books transfer, so call the Treasurer in the last week of April for the amount due. Online payments for delinquent town tax open at the end of April. Mailed payments go to P.O. Box 128, Johnstown, NY 12095, and never as cash.

Fulton County offers one, but only in May. Local Law No. 2 of 1997 lets the Treasurer sign installment agreements with owners of residential real property, and the county processes them only from May 1 through May 31. Letters go out in April to qualified owners who are behind.

  • The down payment is 25% of the eligible delinquent taxes.
  • Payments are monthly, and the term cannot exceed 24 months.
  • Eligible taxes in the most recent window were the prior year's county tax and the school and city tax from the year before that.
  • Commercial property and land are not eligible.
  • A parcel foreclosed on within the last three years, or one that defaulted on an installment agreement in the last three years, is not eligible.

Call the Treasurer to confirm whether you qualify. If you miss this May, the next chance is May 2027. Owners who are behind and thinking of selling should ask about the plan first, since a signed agreement and a written balance make it easier for a title company to close.

The Treasurer's office handles the foreclosure and auction steps, so anyone with a lien that old should call (518) 736-5580 or email fctreasurer@fultoncountyny.gov before listing a house. In the latest round, owners with unpaid school, city and county taxes from several years back were given a last day to redeem, and that date came in November 2025.

The rules for redeeming are the same each round. All taxes must be paid in full in reverse chronological order by year, with guaranteed funds. Ask the Treasurer for a Parcel Status Report to learn the exact amount owed. Owners can pay at the Treasurer's office or by card online. The county also points people toward the New York State Homeowner Assistance Fund for help with delinquent taxes.

sections.h2: What to know about Fulton County housing
sections.html:
Fulton County is in the Mohawk Valley. Johnstown is the county seat and Gloversville is the largest city. Population has slipped from 55,531 in 2010 to an estimated 52,216 in 2025, across 28,418 housing units. Owners live in 71.4% of homes. The typical owner-occupied home is valued at $163,100, typical monthly rent is $912, and median household income is $66,533. Only 85 building permits were recorded in 2025, so new construction is thin and resale homes carry most of the market.

With values in that range, back taxes, interest and fees can eat a large share of a seller's proceeds, which is why checking the Beacon map and the Treasurer's balance before listing pays off.

sections.h2: How do I clear Fulton County tax before closing a sale?
sections.html:
Ask the right office for the right year. During tax collection dates you contact the local tax collector. Outside those dates you contact the County Treasurer for county and town taxes, and the city or school collector for those taxes.

  1. Find the parcel's SBL number on the Beacon map or the tax bill.
  2. Call the Treasurer at (518) 736-5580 and ask for a Parcel Status Report on any delinquent year.
  3. Pay older years first, since the Treasurer requires reverse chronological order for foreclosure redemption.
  4. Ask about exemptions, STAR and veteran or senior benefits through your assessor or the county's real property office at (518) 736-5509. STAR applications go to the state directly.
  5. Give the closing attorney the written payoff amounts.

The Treasurer's office can say which taxing districts are involved when a parcel straddles city, town and school bills. Bring the SBL number, the deed or tax bill, and any installment agreement paperwork when you call or visit. On closing day, the attorney or title company should have a current figure from each office that bills the parcel: the town or county for the early-year tax, the school collector, and the village or city if one applies. A bill paid in the wrong office can be returned, so confirm who holds each year before you send money. Timing matters too. A closing in February or March usually means the town collector still holds the current bill, while a closing after May usually means the Treasurer holds anything left over. A cash buyer who takes the house as it stands can close with the payoff taken from proceeds, which skips the wait for a financed buyer's appraisal and lender review.

faqs.q: When can I pay Fulton County tax to my town collector?
faqs.a: January 1 through March 31. After that the town collector returns unpaid bills to the County Treasurer, and the Treasurer's office begins collections on May 1.

faqs.q: Is there a Fulton County installment plan for back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes, for eligible owners of residential property, but agreements are processed only in May. The down payment is 25% of the eligible delinquent tax, the term is up to 24 months, and payments are monthly.

faqs.q: Does the Fulton County Treasurer collect City of Johnstown taxes?
faqs.a: No. The Treasurer does collect City of Gloversville parcels, but for City of Johnstown taxes you contact the city.

faqs.q: How do I find a Fulton County parcel's tax map number?
faqs.a: Use the Beacon online map from the Real Property Tax Service Agency. It shows the SBL, also called the tax map number, along with ownership and assessed value. The same number appears on tax bills and assessment rolls.

faqs.q: How do I apply for STAR in Fulton County?
faqs.a: Apply directly with New York State. Owners now register with the state, and the state number is (518) 457-2036.
